title: A four sided shape has three right angles: what is the fourth?
description: A four sided shape has three angles of ninety degrees, and the video uses the total of three hundred sixty to find the fourth. Keeko then doubts and says the fourth angle can be any size.
teaching_notes: One idea: the four angles always add to three hundred sixty, so three right angles force the fourth to be a right angle too. Watch for students who think the last angle is free because only three are given.

source: A quadrilateral has three angles of 90°. Find the fourth angle.
video_script.why: The child uses the fixed total of three hundred sixty to see that three right angles force a fourth right angle, and that four right angles make a rectangle.
video_script.substitution: Add the three right angles, take the sum from three hundred sixty, and read the shape from its four angles.
video_script.anchor: a four sided shape with three right angle marks and a question mark at the fourth angle
video_script.wrong_answer: the fourth angle can be any size
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the fourth angle can be any size, because only three angles are given; but the four angles must add to 360 degrees, so 270 + the fourth angle = 360 forces it to be exactly 90.
video_script.payoff_line: The fourth angle is ninety degrees, so the shape is a rectangle

final_answer.value: 90°, so the quadrilateral is a rectangle
final_answer.spoken: the fourth angle is ninety degrees, so the shape is a rectangle

hold_back: so the shape is a rectangle
maths_rules: the four angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360 degrees
a quadrilateral with four right angles is a rectangle
check: if the fourth angle were any other size, the total would not be 360
video_script.design: One idea: the total of 360 degrees leaves only one possible size for the fourth angle. Wrong idea: the fourth angle can be any size. The shape with its three right angles stays on the board.
